name: Two MegaMen a side
now: A side-by-side team match from the Net Square (protocol v15: four seats over the server, ARENA_SEAT, the stands' four streams) and the dev flag's (--dev arena2v2): four MegaMen on BN6's field in the Arena's pair, the partners' keys two more streams of the Arena's input (players 2 and 3), sampled on their side's GBA's frames as its pad is and carried in that GBA's own link packets (the two bytes +5 and +7 BN6 never writes or reads, written at the pad's store 0x0801FF8C and read out of both sides' received packets 0x020399F0), so that both GBAs take a partner's word from the exchange that brings his lead's pad, at the same iteration; guessed and rolled back as the other player's. Each partner has his own battle NaviStats and hand, answered by object; picks his chips on BN6's own Custom screen on a plain copy of the pair his own client keeps, from his own deck, which each GBA deals and keeps from the packets' words alone; the leads wait for him by BN6's own link wait, the limit said in his place by his side's GBA. His whole MegaMan: his NaviCust compiled by BN6's own reload (on every game of a match from the MegaMan he sent), his Crosses and Beast Out on his own screen and run by BN6's crossing for his object, a Program Advance joined in his hand as BN6 joins it; UNITE with his own Souls on his own screen (BN5's installs' hooks on his copy's GBA), his Soul crossing in his stream into his own Souls block, its life, powers and look by object. Under full rules BN5's chip AI's rooms, the Chaos Unison, a Soul's powers and look, BN5's mood and DarkChip rule answer by object. Proved on both GBAs, through rollbacks and mutations, and over a local server with four games and a spectator (a partner never picking, a Cross, a PA, Beast Out with 40 ms lag and 30 ms jitter, a slow partner, a drop).
left: ColonelSoul's button for a partner pressed (built; his ColonelSoul's unison proved), the Dark Soul's lists from his own folder, the green flash's tint and a hit's mood gain by object; a real network, the deployed server, devices; a partner's NaviCust compiled on games of different runs; WhiCapsl's and Uninstll's marks and a chip of computed power in his hand.
